glossary.Inflammation: The body's response to injury or infection, causing swelling and damage.
glossary.Diphtheria: A bacterial throat infection whose toxin can inflame the heart; rare where vaccination is routine.
glossary.Malaise: A general feeling of being unwell.
glossary.MI: Myocardial infarction: heart muscle death from a blocked coronary artery.
glossary.Angina: Chest pain from heart muscle not getting enough oxygen.
glossary.Tachycardia: Heart rate above 100 beats per minute.
glossary.Sinus tachycardia: A normal rhythm from the sinus node, but faster than 100 beats per minute.
glossary.Palpitations: An unpleasant awareness of your own heartbeat.
glossary.Heart failure: The heart cannot pump enough blood to meet the body's needs.
glossary.Flu-like illness: Fever, aches, sore throat and tiredness like influenza.
glossary.CAD: Coronary artery disease: narrowing of the heart's arteries by atherosclerosis.
glossary.Risk factors: Things that make a disease more likely, such as smoking or diabetes for heart disease.
glossary.HIV: Human immunodeficiency virus, which weakens the immune system and can inflame the heart.
glossary.Systolic dysfunction: The ventricle cannot squeeze properly, so less blood is pumped out.
glossary.Gallop: A heart rhythm with an extra sound, like a galloping horse.
glossary.ST elevation: The ST segment raised above baseline on the ECG.
glossary.T wave inversion: A T wave that points downwards on the ECG.
glossary.STEMI: ST-elevation myocardial infarction: a heart attack from a fully blocked coronary artery.
glossary.Diffuse: Spread widely rather than confined to one area.
glossary.Non-specific: A finding that could fit many conditions, so does not point to one.
glossary.Oedema: Swelling from excess fluid in the tissue.
glossary.Echo: Echocardiogram: an ultrasound scan of the heart.
glossary.Biopsy: Taking a small tissue sample to look at under a microscope.
glossary.Supportive: Treatment that supports the body while it recovers, rather than curing the cause.
glossary.ACE inhibitor: Drug that blocks angiotensin II formation, used in heart failure.
glossary.Beta-blocker: Drug that slows the heart and protects it in heart failure.
glossary.Diuretics: Water tablets that make the kidneys remove extra fluid.
glossary.Occlusive: Caused by a blockage of a vessel.
glossary.Myocytes: Muscle cells; here heart muscle cells.
glossary.T-cells: White blood cells that attack infected or abnormal cells.
glossary.Bystander myocytes: Healthy heart cells near infected ones that get damaged by the immune attack.
glossary.Necrosis: Death of cells in living tissue.
glossary.Conduction: The spread of the electrical signal through the heart.
glossary.Hyperaemia: Increased blood flow to a tissue, a sign of inflammation.
glossary.Gadolinium: A contrast agent given for MRI that collects in damaged or scarred tissue.
glossary.Mid-wall: The middle layer of the heart muscle wall.
glossary.Myocardial workload: How hard the heart muscle has to work, rising with heart rate and BP.
glossary.Coronary artery territory: The area of heart muscle supplied by one coronary artery.
glossary.Scar: Fibrous tissue replacing dead heart muscle.
